title: 'Go Sell Ice Cream': AR Rahman Answers Ramayana Song Critics With a Steve Jobs Line
excerpt: Facing backlash over 'Mangal Rang', the Ramayana composer told Screen he is his own first critic, that tunes mature like pickles, and that pleasing everyone was never the brief, three days before the film opens.
body:
• A.R. Rahman has answered criticism of 'Mangal Rang', a song from Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, quoting Steve Jobs: "If you want to satisfy everyone, go sell ice cream."
  • In an interview with Screen, Rahman said he is his own first critic and that some tunes improve with time: "Like pickle, for certain tunes, the older it is, the better it becomes."
  • 'Mangal Rang', sung by Arijit Singh and Shreya Ghoshal with lyrics by Kumar Vishwas, drew objections online for its qawwali-like treatment in a mythological epic.
  • The Hindi film, directed by Nitesh Tiwari with music by Rahman and Hans Zimmer, opens in theatres on November 5, 2026.

A.R. Rahman does not intend to compose by referendum. Responding to the mixed, and in places hostile, reaction to 'Mangal Rang', the first song from Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, the composer borrowed a line from Steve Jobs in an interview with Screen: "If you want to satisfy everyone, go sell ice cream."

What he actually said

Rahman's defense was about process, not defiance. "I am my first critic. It is not that I just love everything I do," he told Screen. "We don't decide something in a day. We live with it for months sometimes. There's a thought process." He argued that some compositions disclose themselves slowly: "Sometimes you need to take anthropology into consideration. Sometimes, you let something be, like pickle: for certain tunes, the older it is, the better it becomes."

"If you want to satisfy everyone, go sell ice cream."

— A.R. Rahman, quoting Steve Jobs, in Screen

Why this song drew fire

'Mangal Rang', sung by Arijit Singh and Shreya Ghoshal with lyrics by Kumar Vishwas, sits inside a film retelling the Ramayana, and a section of listeners objected to its Sufi-qawwali coloring for material they expected to hear treated devotionally. The argument has run for days on social media, which is precisely the instant-verdict cycle Rahman is pushing back against. He also spoke in the same interview about composing the film's score alongside Hans Zimmer, a collaboration he has said could draw international attention to the project.

The film around the argument

Ramayana: Rise of a Legend is a Hindi-language epic directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra, starring Ranbir Kapoor as Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana and Sunny Deol as Hanuman. The first part reaches theatres worldwide on November 5, 2026, three days from now, with the second part slated for Diwali 2027. Whether 'Mangal Rang' ages like the pickle of Rahman's analogy is a question the film's release, and time, will answer. His point stands either way: the verdict he is waiting for is not opening-weekend social media.
